Tariffs on Canadian auto parts increase costs at every border crossing, making Canadian production less competitive. Over 500,000 Canadian jobs depend on the auto sector directly and indirectly. The US has imposed tariffs on Canadian softwood lumber repeatedly over decades, claiming Canadian stumpage fees constitute unfair subsidies. Each round of tariffs devastates Canadian forestry communities — primarily in British Columbia, Quebec, and Ontario. No advanced economy sends 75% of its exports to one country. Canada's trade dependence on the US is unique among G7 nations. This dependence was not inevitable — it was the result of policy choices: proximity, NAFTA/CUSMA integration, failure to develop alternative markets, and pipeline politics that prevented tidewater access for energy exports.
